skill.name: biogeobears
skill.description: Set up reproducible BioGeoBEARS workflows for phylogenetic biogeography. The skill validates tree and geography inputs, reformats distribution data, generates RMarkdown analysis files, and guides model comparison and visualization.
skill.summary: Prepare, validate, and document BioGeoBEARS ancestral range analyses in R.
skill.author: brunoasm

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown or R Markdown code fences, inline R expressions, documentation links, and expected relative paths. The confirmed static risk is an unrestricted file write in the validation script, and a semantic supply-chain concern exists because the skill recommends unpinned GitHub package installation. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The geography validator writes to any user-supplied output path.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve output paths against the intended analysis directory, reject parent traversal, and warn before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The setup instructions install BioGeoBEARS from an unpinned GitHub repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a commit or release, document the expected source, and ask users to confirm before installing external R packages.

remediation.issue: The workflow includes documented shell and R commands that create files and run analysis scripts.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should run only after user confirmation and inside a dedicated project directory.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic biogeography workflows can be hard to format and reproduce. This skill validates inputs, prepares BioGeoBEARS scripts, and guides model comparison in R.
actual_capabilities: Validates PHYLIP-like geography files and checks species names against tree tips.
Reformats CSV or TSV distribution tables into BioGeoBEARS geography format.
Generates an organized analysis folder with input, scripts, results, and documentation.
Customizes an RMarkdown template for DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and +J models.
Produces model comparison tables, ancestral range plots, and HTML report instructions.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for formatting, rooting, convergence, and runtime issues.
limitations: Users must install R, BioGeoBEARS, Python 3, and supporting R packages separately.
Large trees or many geographic areas can take hours to run.
The skill prepares workflows but does not guarantee biological model suitability.
Excel files may need export to CSV or TSV before the bundled validator can reformat them.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Ancestral Range Study
use_cases.description: Set up validated inputs, scripts, and documentation for a phylogenetic biogeography analysis.

use_cases.title: Teach Reproducible BioGeoBEARS Workflows
use_cases.description: Create a clear folder structure and guided analysis steps for students learning historical biogeography.

use_cases.title: Check Data Before Model Fitting
use_cases.description: Find tree and geography mismatches before running long BioGeoBEARS optimization jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with known input files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a BioGeoBEARS analysis. My tree file is [tree path], my distribution file is [data path], and I have [number] areas.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Geography Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a table and check species names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate my geography file against this phylogenetic tree. Reformat it for BioGeoBEARS if needed, and explain any species mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Models and Parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan model comparison before running R.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend BioGeoBEARS models and maximum range size for [taxon group] across [area list]. Explain the tradeoffs before generating scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Publication Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible BioGeoBEARS workflow with validation, model comparison, ancestral range plots, README notes, and interpretation guidance for publication.

output_examples.input: A researcher provides a rooted tree and a species-by-region distribution table.
output: The skill validates species names and geography encoding.
It prepares a project folder with inputs, an RMarkdown analysis, results paths, and a README.
It explains how to run the analysis and review the HTML report.

output_examples.input: A user asks which model best explains island bird distributions.
output: The skill recommends comparing DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and +J variants.
It prepares model comparison tables using AIC, AICc, and likelihood ratio tests.
It describes how to interpret dispersal, extinction, and founder-event estimates.

best_practices: Validate tree and geography files before generating the final analysis script.
Keep original input files separate from reformatted BioGeoBEARS inputs.
Report model uncertainty when AIC weights are similar across models.
anti_patterns: Do not run all models before checking species names and tree rooting.
Do not choose maximum range size only because it is computationally convenient.
Do not treat the best AIC model as biologically correct without domain review.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a rooted Newick tree and a geography table with species names and presence or absence by area.

faq.question: Can it run BioGeoBEARS by itself?
faq.answer: It prepares scripts and instructions. The user still needs R, BioGeoBEARS, and required packages installed.

faq.question: Which models can it set up?
faq.answer: It supports DEC, DEC+J, DIVALIKE, DIVALIKE+J, BAYAREALIKE, and BAYAREALIKE+J workflows.

faq.question: Does it validate species names?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled Python validator can compare geography species names against tree tip labels.

faq.question: How are results presented?
faq.answer: The RMarkdown template creates model tables, parameter summaries, ancestral range plots, and an HTML report.

faq.question: What are the main limits?
faq.answer: Runtime can be long for large datasets, and biological assumptions still require expert review.
